comments.author: OkVariety8064
comments.body:
> I signed up to develop a game not to be a pixel artist. 

In game development, no single asset is the goal, the game itself is. But then again, those component parts of games are creative expression in themselves for other people.

Is it OK to use AI for parts that are not core to your expression? But where do you even draw the line? If someone managed to do everything you do, including the game design, with agents, every last little part without human intervention, would that be reasonable? I don't know.

> Is it still justified to use Gen AI in that case for all the art assets? 

I don't know, I really don't. Even the legal questions aren't settled. At the very least, those assets are not copyrightable (unless modified).

From an ethical point of view, the model was trained on everything it could rip off, including all classic pixel art games, art sites like Pixel Joint and so on. Did those people consent to a machine using their personal creative expression as a template from which to generate more?

It would be so, so very much easier if there were proper generative AI models trained on only copyright-free works. Public domain, creative commons and so on. You could still argue about how desirable such things are, but that would be more a philosophical issue, without the elephant in the room of generative AI "stealing" copyrighted creative expression to automatically generate more such expression to compete with the original expression.

> Is it still justified to rely on Claude for coding? 

Personally, I can't see the issue with AI coding. Code was never art, it's a functional thing, and there are only so many ways to express a given algorithm. Sure, the copyright issue still exists, but I can't see a code generator being personal in the same way as an art generator.

replies.author: TPM2209
replies.body:
It's more the senior developers who have their own projects that they've wanted to do but never had the time for. They're usually more like architects at that point, which is where AI coding tools shine the most.

You never have to focus on the actual implementation ever again, except in the few-in-a-million edge cases where the AI gets stuck on something genuinely novel. Some people love that, others hate it.
